name_reason: Conforms to data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> with the battle-core data_fd2_battle_* prefix; descriptor 'pathfind_mode_flags' accurately reflects role (a scalar control byte selecting the neighbor-step commit policy) and matches the rest of the pathfind global family. No Ghidra address residue. 'flags' is a conventional descriptor for a mode/policy byte even though it is read as enum-like equality probes (0/1/2) rather than bit-tested; acceptable and already documented as 'mode flags' in src.
purpose: Single unsigned byte selecting the neighbor-step commit policy for the path-aware destination search (mode 0 standard / 1 standard+direction-diversity tiebreak / 2 ignore-obstacles+destination-record).
logic_summary: Written 8-bit once per search by fd2_pathfind_to_destination from its mode_flags (md) argument: low byte of [EBP+0x24] stored via MOV [0x6017A],AL @ 0x4E1E6. The plain flood-fill orchestrator fd2_init_movement_range_floodfill never sets it. Read 8-bit unsigned by fd2_pathfind_neighbor_step_with_tiebreak as two small-constant equality probes: on a cost tie the direction-diversity tiebreak is attempted only when value==1 (CMP [0x6017A],1 @ 0x4E35B; JNZ skip), and the ignore-obstacles + destination-record branch is taken only when value==2 (CMP [0x6017A],2 @ 0x4E385; JNZ fall to the passability-gated modes 0/1 path). Write-before-read: the orchestrator sets it before any reader runs, so the load value (0) is never observed.
element_semantics: Enum-like mode selector: 0 = standard (strictly-better commits, ties never win); 1 = standard + direction-diversity tiebreak; 2 = ignore-obstacles + destination-record. Not an array (adjacent nonzero bytes belong to separate globals).
notes: src comment block (pathfnd.c lines ~920-936) already precise and matches disassembly (write @0x4E1E6, reads @0x4E35B/0x4E385, modes 0/1/2, scalar/not-array, write-before-read); no src Edit needed -> comment_verdict=keep. Ghidra data plate was empty (<null>); created a concise plate via PLATE_COMMENT reflecting the src conclusion and saved the program. is_const=false because the game has a WRITE xref (0x4E1E6). xrefs confirmed: 1 WRITE (fd2_pathfind_to_destination @0x4E1E6), 2 READ (fd2_pathfind_neighbor_step_with_tiebreak @0x4E35B, @0x4E385).
